extracted.intended_audience: state agency rulemaking staff, agency general counsel, and officials responsible for New York State rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for preparing, filing, and publishing Notices of Adoption, emergency adoptions, incorporations by reference, Regulatory Agendas, and five-year reviews under New York State rulemaking (SAPA/Executive Law) procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency certification for adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: A signed certification (on agency letterhead) by an authorized official certifying that the attached amendment to the NYCRR was duly adopted pursuant to the specified authority, stating the date of adoption and the effective date (specify date, time frame OR 'upon publication of a Notice of Adoption in the State Register'), and indicating the State Register publication ID number for the notice of proposed rule making (if applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include typed name, title, signature, and date. If other prior notice was required by statute, include the publication date(s) and manner of publication. Use the Department of State adoption certification sample; electronic (scanned PDF) or hard-copy original may be submitted. For authorities/boards/commissions/public benefit corporations, certify vote/members present as applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency adoption findings requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If adopting on an emergency basis, the agency must state that immediate adoption is necessary for preservation of the public health, safety, or general welfare and must state the specific reasons underlying that finding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do NOT paraphrase SAPA §202; state the entity’s factual findings and reasons. The certification should indicate emergency adoption authorized by SAPA §202(6) and whether effective immediately upon filing. You may submit a separate statement of findings provided it is certified by the agency head as reflecting the findings made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Action taken (Item 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the action taken as a reiteration of the 'Proposed action' from the original Notice of Proposed Rule Making or the modified version published with a Notice of Revised Rule Making (e.g., adds, amends, renumbers, repeals, and specify which rule/Part/section).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter a short statement indicating whether the action adds, amends, renumbers, or repeals the rule and specify the Part/section of NYCRR affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Effective date (Item 2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify an effective date for the newly adopted rule; the form allows checking a box for publication-effective rules or specifying a future date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most rules are effective upon publication of a Notice of Adoption; if effective on filing or a future date, specify that in the certification. For emergency adoptions, delete the standard Item 1 effective-date language if effective immediately upon filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Statutory authority, subject and purpose (Items 3-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the exact language published in the original Notice of Proposed Rule Making for statutory authority, subject, and purpose unless changes to the rule affect such language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not alter the previously published authority/subject/purpose language unless the rule changes require revision; if revised, attach the revised statement as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Terms (text) and identification of rule (Item 6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the I.D. No. of the original notice; indicate whether the text changed (no change, nonsubstantial changes, or changes to rates/wages/etc.) and attach appropriate adopted text or summaries as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A. Enter original ID No.; B. Check first box if no changes to text — do not attach unchanged text; if nonsubstantial changes, check second box, identify location of changes and attach adopted text (full text if originally submitted full text; summary if originally submitted summary). Complete Items 9-12 and attach revised statements or explain why not attached. Note: you must submit electronic or hard-copy certification and text for NYCRR publication whether or not text/substance is submitted for State Register. Hard copies must be received in DAR the same day you e-file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Items 9-12 (Revised RIS, RFA, RAFA, JIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: If previously published Regulatory Impact Statement (RIS), Regulatory Flexibility Analysis (RFA), Rural Area Flexibility Analysis (RAFA), or Job Impact Statement (JIS) remains adequate, you may skip Items 9-12; otherwise attach a revised statement or explain why a revised statement is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section A — when attaching a revised statement, indicate whether attachment is full text or a summary. Section B — if text changed and you attach an explanation why a revised statement is not required, check the appropriate box. Section C — check if the rule is a 'rate making' to indicate certain exemptions. Note: a JIS is not required for the State Comptroller or Attorney General.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Assessment of public comment (Item 13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach an assessment of public comment (including legislative comment) received since the proposal was published; you may address only those comments received since the last published proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not reiterate a previously published assessment; limit the assessment to new comments. This assessment must be attached with the Notice of Adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Adoption — Referenced material (Item 14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether the rule includes material incorporated by reference and, if so, specify where in the text the references are located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Chapter 5 'How to Incorporate by Reference' for identification, filing, availability, and copyright certification requirements. Tick the appropriate box on the form and provide required information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Certification completion
rubrics_metrics.description: The person who prepared the Notice of Adoption form must complete the Agency Certification, certifying that the form and attachments comply with applicable SAPA and Department of State requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By signing the certification you attest that you have reviewed the form and that the notice complies with all applicable provisions. The certifier should be knowledgeable about the submission and its compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption package for NYCRR and State Register
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption is printed in two separate publications; for NYCRR you must attach a scanned copy of signed certification (pdf) plus the full text of the rule (with bracketing/underlining if needed) in Word format; for the State Register, e-file the Notice of Adoption form (DAR will print from e-filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard copy original certification with full text attached can be submitted in lieu of electronic submission (original and two copies). Use the paper-clip feature on the e-form to attach documents. Ensure hard copies are received in DAR same day you e-file if submitting hard copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of adoption hard copies and notice to officers
rubrics_metrics.description: If not submitting certification and text electronically, deliver hard-copy certification with original signature attached to the text of the rule plus two copies to DAR (address provided). At the same time, send each '202(6-a)' and '101-a' officer a copy of the notice along with full text and attachments as required by Exec Law §101-a and SAPA §202(6-a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DAR address: Department of State, One Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Ave., Suite 650, Albany, NY 12231-0001. Office hours 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday–Friday. See Appendix D for specific officer addresses and instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgment of filing
rubrics_metrics.description: You will receive two e-mail acknowledgments for each rule making: an automatic acknowledgement from the West Group Data Capture system confirming whether your e-filing succeeded or failed (sent immediately), and a second acknowledgement from DAR after processing that includes the assigned identification number and NYCRR citation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The first e-mail is critical—DAR is not notified of e-filing failures, so confirm success. The second e-mail is sent to the person who certified the rule making form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changing a newly adopted rule
rubrics_metrics.description: After a rule is filed and before its effective date, you may amend, suspend or repeal a rule in situations where such action does not constitute a substantial revision to the rule [SAPA §203(2)].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the rule is effective upon publication of a Notice of Adoption (most rules), you have only a limited time to submit an Amended Notice of Adoption. E-file the Amended Notice of Adoption and notify the '202(6-a)' and '101-a' officers if you amend a newly adopted rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency rule overview and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Emergency rule making allows adoption on a temporary basis (maximum 90 days initially) when immediate adoption is necessary for preservation of public health, safety, or general welfare and compliance with the normal proposal process would be contrary to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emergency may be re-adopted (each re-adoption effective for a maximum of 60 days) but each re-adoption requires initiation of the regular proposal process for permanent adoption. Emergency rules may be effective on filing date or a future specified date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Adoption forms and combination with proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the Notice of Emergency Adoption to adopt on an emergency basis alone, or the Notice of Emergency Adoption and Proposed Rule Making form to adopt the emergency and initiate the proposal process simultaneously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If agency is subject to Executive Chamber rule review, obtain approval before submitting a Notice of Emergency Adoption and Proposed Rule Making. The proposal portion of the combined form is subject to the same requirements and calendaring issues as any proposal; you may need Notice of Revised Rule Making during the proposal period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency adoption filing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file a certification and the full text of the rule (with bracketing/underlining to show amendments) when e-filing a Notice of Emergency Adoption or the combined emergency/proposal form, with all applicable attachments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For samples and special instructions refer to Chapter 3. If combining emergency with proposal, follow proposal requirements concurrently. Hard copies may be submitted in lieu of electronic submission (original and two copies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency Adoption package (attachments and e-filing)
rubrics_metrics.description: For NYCRR: attach a scanned copy of signed certification (pdf) and the full text of the rule in MS Word before e-filing; for the State Register: e-file the Notice of Emergency Adoption (DAR will print from e-filing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No hard copies of form and attachments are required for the State Register e-filing. Use the paper-clip 'add' feature to include attachments. If submitting hard copy, deliver on same day you e-file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery and notice to Exec L 101-a and SAPA 202(6-a) officers for emergencies
rubrics_metrics.description: When filing an emergency adoption, send each Exec. L. 101-a and SAPA 202(6-a) officer a copy of the notice along with the full text of the rule and full text of every attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix D contains e-mail and mailing addresses and complete instructions for these officers. Deliver hard copies to DAR if not e-filing; see adoption delivery guidance for address and hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on changing emergency rules
rubrics_metrics.description: You may only amend, suspend or repeal a newly adopted emergency rule before it becomes effective if the change does not constitute a substantial revision; emergencies cannot be withdrawn, and most emergency rules are effective upon filing and therefore cannot be amended after effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an emergency specified a future effective date and you file a Notice of Amended Adoption before that date, amendment is theoretically possible. Otherwise you must wait for expiration (or adopt a new emergency measure to supersede the prior one) or initiate the proposal process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — filing and availability requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: State agencies may incorporate outside publications by reference into NYCRR only if the publication is precisely identified in the rule and filed with the Department of State; copies must be available for public use and inspection at designated agency offices, the Department of State, the Legislative Library, and four designated Supreme Court law libraries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit the required copies to DOS until you formally adopt the rule. Provide copies to RRU for Executive Chamber review along with proposals when applicable. Photocopies are acceptable for public comment purposes. Ensure availability to regulated parties and obtain copyright certification that reproduction and distribution will not violate copyright.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by reference — identification requirements (Exec. L. §102(1)(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: The text of the rule must include an accurate and complete description of every publication incorporated by reference, including: title/name; edition or volume; page/section numbers (if applicable); author/editor; publisher name and address; date of publication; and location (adopting agency address or DOS) where the publication may be viewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be precise in citations; inaccurate citations may lead DOS to certify no record on file. Include sufficient locating information for the public to access the publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporated material and 2,000-word publication limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Text of incorporated material is not counted when determining whether the text of a proposal or adoption is 2,000 words or more; a summary of text must be submitted for publication in the State Register only if the rule text (excluding referenced material) is 2,000 words or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing summaries or full text for the State Register, exclude incorporated-by-reference material from the word count calculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referencing previously filed publications (re-ref)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the publication to be incorporated is already on file with DOS (filed by your agency or another), you need not file additional copies so long as the rule is accompanied by a statement precisely identifying the previously filed publication, including DOS file number and date filed (and filing agency if different).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Call DOS to verify if a document is on file and obtain file information. Provide precise identification to enable DOS to locate the previously filed material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparing publications for filing — copies, format, and labeling
rubrics_metrics.description: You must file two copies of the original bound publication with DOS, one copy with the Legislative Library, and one copy with each of the four designated Supreme Court law libraries (Supreme Court libraries require electronic form meeting 22 NYCRR 123).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For permanently bound volumes deliver two copies; for soft-bound under 100 pages, place one copy in a rigid-cover binder (no ring binders). Loose-leaf materials may be filed in a publisher-manufactured binder. Affix an adhesive label in the upper-left corner of the front cover with publication name, edition/volume number/title, author/editor, and date of publication. Federal Register/CFR materials may be downloaded and bound for filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporation by Reference Certification form requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A form completed by the agency's general counsel must state the publication details, identify the NYCRR sections referencing the material, opine that the referenced publication is reasonably available to regulated parties, and opine that reproduction and distribution will not violate copyright; indicate whether the original or a paper reproduction is being submitted and certify accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form fields include: Publication title, volume/section/pages, author, publication date, publisher name/address, electronic location/source; NYCRR title and sections where referenced; factual basis for availability opinion; factual basis for copyright opinion; checkbox indicating original submission or paper reproduction and certification that the paper reproduction was supervised and is a true and accurate reproduction. General Counsel must sign, date, and provide title/agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda — required contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Every Regulatory Agenda must include a list and brief description of the subject matter of all rules being considered for rule making, and the name, public office, address, telephone number (and may include e-mail) of an agency representative knowledgeable about the rule making who can provide information and receive comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify each rule for which a Regulatory Flexibility Analysis or Rural Area Flexibility Analysis may be required, and provide outreach to potentially affected small businesses, local governments, and public or private interests located in rural areas for those rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory Agenda — format, submission, and publication schedule
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulatory Agendas must be typed in the prescribed format (Word or WordPerfect) and e-mailed to NYSRegister@dos.ny.gov with 'Regulatory Agenda' in the subject line; agendas are published twice a year in the first January and the last June issues of the State Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines vary each year but generally have to be ready by mid-December for the January issue and mid-June for the June issue; DOS accepts agendas during the three submission weeks prior to the issue deadline. E-mail or submit/hard-deliver to Department of State, Division of Administrative Rules (physical address provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory and discretionary Regulatory Agenda publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain agencies (Division of Housing and Community Renewal; Workers’ Compensation Board; departments of Agriculture and Markets, Education, Environmental Conservation, Financial Services, Health, Labor, Motor Vehicles and State; and the offices of Children and Family Services, and Temporary and Disability Assistance) must publish semi-annual Regulatory Agendas in the State Register. Other agencies may publish at their discretion, using the same deadlines and information requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency specified by the Governor or the Governor’s designee may also be required to publish. Discretionary agendas follow the same submission rules and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuously updated Regulatory Agenda option
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency that publishes its Regulatory Agenda on its website may maintain a continuously updated Regulatory Agenda, adding descriptions when the agency begins to consider a rule and removing them when the agency is no longer considering the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a description is newly listed, conspicuously indicate it has been newly listed for at least 30 days and identify the date first listed. Agencies that maintain continuously updated agendas on their websites need not publish in the last June issue; the January agenda must inform the public of the website and address. Information concerning continuously updated agendas must be republished in the last June issue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to send Regulatory Agendas
rubrics_metrics.description: E-mail (preferred), mail, or hand-deliver Regulatory Agendas to the Department of State, Division of Administrative Rules; e-mail: nysregister@dos.ny.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical address: Department of State, Division of Administrative Rules, One Commerce Plaza, 99 Washington Avenue, Suite 650, Albany, NY 12231-0001. Use the prescribed electronic format and subject line when e-mailing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five-year review requirement for existing rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rule adopted on or after January 1, 1997 shall be reviewed after five years and, thereafter, at five-year intervals unless another law specifically provides otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain procedures and schedules to ensure each rule is reviewed on the five-year cycle; this is a mandatory requirement under SAPA unless otherwise provided.
